# Native Live workspace and stability

`make linux-live-stability-test` and `make linux-fluid-workspace-test` now depend on one native `linux-live-workspace-test`. It runs the shared application/command owners, then the existing conversation/document owners. Requesting both aliases executes those owners once. No Python preparation or interpreter is needed; real offline diagrams require WebKitGTK 6.0 in addition to the documented application runner dependencies.

The immutable reference is untouched v1.6.0, commit `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Temporary observers import the external downloaded release, verify imported source against that commit, and drive its actual application or component. The application observer also verifies all 77 released modules before activation and checks imported paths/digests again after shutdown. No application handler, scheduler or renderer is replaced. Native tests consume the static observations below; collectors stay under ignored `tmp/` and do not run from Make or ship.

| Independent fixture | Added observations | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Assembled Live workspace](released-application-live-workspace.json) | 22 states, four layouts, four speech requests, three Codex turns and a reopened reply texture | `ab648aa61ae379ba72ef4012cf3b26116e013e39d8caa7cfc479c6f496199c87` |
| [Live stability](released-live-stability.json) | Ten GTK/frame-clock states | `3e8409c006e8c0511ad94bed7d129e46caf33d7a7d6fe355c778a396ad12e3f7` |
| [Diagram transitions](released-diagram-transitions.json) | Nine actual WebKit render/failure states | `8be15611c95147121a37cc21af1c1d243ea4d296601a18a3c0d905b94006578d` |

The shared assembled application now covers eleven workflows/122 states. Existing application, command and continuation fixtures are unchanged. The conversation owner reaches 123 page/scroll/stability states, and the document owner reaches fifteen actual render states. Existing fence/XML/forecast and lossless Questions checks retain their separate ordinary coverage.

The application scenario uses actual `ApplicationDesktop` services, GTK buttons/buffers, private Ctrl+P/Return input, clipboard and compatible SQLite/config stores. Native PCM and Codex processes plus loopback HTTP supply only microphone/provider boundaries. A real gated preview produces Questions and a flowchart, a template change updates the completed draft, and a second change preserves a deliberate edit. Pausing cancels a gated third turn; releasing it cannot publish over that edit. Presentation settings persist while provider changes are refused during recording. Stop saves the paused draft without copying or stealing the browsed History entry. Reopening the saved reply renders its stored Mermaid. Two silent captures preserve the selected conversation or deliberate draft; a new capture with Live initially disabled seeds its own draft when enabled, then keeps a same-capture edit through another template change.

Four speech request bodies retain exact WAV byte counts and SHA-256 values. All three Codex requests retain complete input, model and effort; two complete, the third is cancelled. Generated entry IDs share a stable mapping, and the seeded History date is fixed to `2026-10-01T13:45:00+00:00` in both stores. No source text, provider prompt, saved draft, preference, notice or clipboard value is normalized away. Shared shutdown acknowledges platform closure, reaps PCM/provider children and removes ephemeral provider workspaces. The test releases its final application references while the GLib loop still runs, allowing asynchronous WebKit teardown to finish.

The stability extension uses real GTK adjustments and frame clocks with animations enabled: 48 source updates at 35 ms intervals must produce intermediate forward motion, no reversal greater than one pixel and real overflow. One hundred identical updates must leave extent/position/margin unchanged. Independent states preserve pane bounds, immediate opaque draft corrections, visible shortened recognition and a fresh capture at the origin. Earlier page cases intentionally hide panes; the new scenario restores both through their actual toggle buttons before starting.

The rendering extension observes real GDK textures, WebKit resource loads, completed render messages and the actual ephemeral network session. Paragraph-only edits must reuse the same texture without a new render; a changed sequence produces the independently recorded replacement. Invalid/directive content preserves editable source, remote image markup starts no HTTP(S) request, and an unfinished fence hides the preview without losing source. Calling WebKit's public process-termination API removes the real renderer and restores editable source. No replacement SVG, mocked timeout or production test API supplies these results.

## Retired checks and retained owners

The deleted Python scripts were called only by their Make targets: `live_stability_smoke.py` had 150 lines and `fluid_workspace_smoke.py` had 301. Relevant behavior history includes `771c867` (Grilling), `a4cf1a6` (motion), `2b7a8b3` (stability), `bf5b297` (silence) and `4bcf12a` (continuation). Their shared helpers still have other consumers and are retained.

| Former contract | Native owner and observable result |
| --- | --- |
| Draft pane before the first response, fresh top origin | Assembled `waiting-for-speech`/`waiting-for-first-draft`; stability `empty-panes`, `first-words`, `fresh-capture` |
| Rapid source growth, identical updates, correction opacity and stable geometry | Stability frame samples, extents, pane bounds, buffer text/tags and `short-correction` |
| Late Live enable uses the current capture; same-capture restart preserves edits | Actual `new-capture-live-off`, `late-live-enable`, `same-capture-template-keeps-edit` |
| Live/history navigation, updated Questions, manual edits and template changes | Actual `history-during-recording`, `return-to-live`, `questions-updated`, `manual-edit`, `template-keeps-edit`; retained conversation and Live owners cover later updates while browsing |
| Searchable settings, persisted placement/time format, active-provider refusal | Actual command keys, persisted/current preferences and refused busy provider change; retained application-shell catalog/settings/deep-link comparison |
| Paused draft saved without copying or late replacement; History selection retained | Actual third-turn cancellation, `late-result-rejected`, `paused-final-preserves-history`, saved reply and unchanged clipboard; retained Live owner also covers paused finalization while viewing Live |
| Silence preserves History or manual draft and adds no recording/result | Both actual silent captures and complete History/documents/clipboard observations; existing capture owner retains status/readiness/failure checks |
| Lossless flow/sequence, paragraph cache reuse, invalid/directive/remote/unfinished input | Root flowchart plus document transition source/visible text, actual textures, render receipts and network observations |
| Saved reply rendering, dark rerender, narrow controls, renderer failure recovery | Root reopened texture and four layouts; actual WebKit termination restores source in the document owner |

The lower-level Live/capture owners retain distinct frozen-prompt, transport, reconciliation, finalization, privacy, store-failure and exit coverage. This conversion extends canonical owners instead of introducing another full application scaffold. No production code changes in this checkpoint. Make changes are +4/-9 lines; test/runner/support changes are +746/-465, including the 451 deleted Python lines. The three independent JSON fixtures add 2,217 lines; documentation is counted separately.

## Recorded execution and review

The old Make route fails the positively verified interpreter trap in `tmp/native-live-before-make.log`. The converted actual command `make linux-live-stability-test linux-fluid-workspace-test` passes with `/usr/bin/python3` and `uv` blocked in `tmp/native-live-final-make.log`, outer session `tmp/native-live-final-make-evidence/session.y8LbKU/`. Application evidence is under `tmp/application/run.ieZ97n/session.gNbBmY/`; component evidence is under `tmp/application/run.6i8NFe/session.9z42tT/`. Every native owner runs without using either trap.

The final released application collection is `tmp/native-live-final-reference.log` and `tmp/native-live-final-reference-evidence/session.sPiOxO/released-live-workspace-1qzoor1w/`. The stability and diagram reference logs are `tmp/native-live-stability-reference.log` and `tmp/native-diagram-transitions-reference-2.log`. All four full-window X11 images match the final native Make run with zero differing pixels: wide/sidebar/dark at 1060×780 and narrow at 480×640. `tmp/native-live-final-pixels.log` records the metrics; recorded control bounds, focus, texture dimensions and PNG hashes also match. This is evidence for these four observed states at this renderer/scale, not every animation or platform.

Review corrected observer/setup issues rather than app behavior: Codex strips a trailing newline; an unfinished Mermaid fence hides the preview without publishing a render; a reused page initially had hidden panes; and the reference timezone must be selected before Python imports. An earlier compact capture differed only in the Home focus ring. Fresh focus observations and both final captures match, without changing production focus behavior. The first application test hung during WebKit thread-exit cleanup; its captured stack identified a missing main-loop teardown interval in the test. Releasing the test-owned app and pumping the loop resolves that exit, with weak ownership checked. These are not claimed as production repairs.

Final actual `make test` passes 139 tests, zero failures and 68 ignored environment checks across 98 suites, both strict all-target Clippy configurations, formatting and generated-document consistency. The relevant ignored application and component checks are explicitly executed by the Make run above. Actual `make linux-python-test` passes 571 tests plus Ruff and formatting for 156 files. Full ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Logs are `tmp/native-live-final-native.log`, `tmp/native-live-final-python.log`, `tmp/native-live-final-gates.log` and `tmp/native-live-final-gates-evidence/session.Oxs5FD/`. No hosted or paid CI is used.

The environment is private X11/Openbox, GTK 4.22.4, Pango 1.58.2, Libadwaita 1.9.3, WebKitGTK 6.0 2.52.6, scale 1 and software Mesa. HOME/XDG, session/accessibility buses, network/PID/mount namespaces and clipboard are isolated; system bus and physical input/audio/GPU devices are masked. Both implementations retain the narrow GtkText width warning and the diagram window's 200-pixel request/207-pixel minimum warning. Reference capture emits the existing GdkX11 deprecation warning; the Python gate retains its PyGObject deprecation warning.

Installed app/widget remain verified 1.6.0. The authorized three-model lineup and default Qwen3-ASR 1.7B are unchanged. Joined compatible/local Live and image contexts, page-driven provisioning, full Command/Notes/Meeting/screenshot workflows, private Wayland/Omarchy behavior, physical keys/microphone/target delivery, broader layout/theme/scale, clean distribution, final maintained Python removal and remaining performance measurements still require acceptance. All whole-workflow rows remain Pending. No replacement, merge or Rust release is authorized by this checkpoint.
